args.sql:
with cogs as (select sku, sum(cost) c from supplies group by sku),
it as (select i.sku from items i join orders o on o.id=i.order_id join stores s on s.id=o.store_id where s.name='Brooklyn' and o.ordered_at>='2025-01-01' and o.ordered_at<'2026-01-01')
select sum(coalesce(c.c,0))/100.0 as total_cost, sum(p.price)/100.0 as sales, 1 - sum(coalesce(c.c,0))*1.0/sum(p.price) as gm, count(*) as n, count(c.c) as m,
(select sum(subtotal)/100.0 from orders o join stores s on s.id=o.store_id where s.name='Brooklyn' and year(ordered_at)=2025) as sub
from it join products p on p.sku=it.sku left join cogs c on c.sku=it.sku

args.message: In 2025, Brooklyn's 178,840 units sold cost $260,822.55 in supplies. Its pre-tax product sales were $1,263,176.00, so the gross margin is about 79.35% (0.7935184408190149). Supply cost per unit is the sum of supplies.cost for each SKU. Sales are the product price summed over every item sold, and this total matches Brooklyn's 2025 order subtotal exactly.
